Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
" *

Adds all the elements of the given arrays into a new array.

*

The new array contains all of the element of array1 followed * by all of the elements array2. When an array is returned, it is always * a new array.

* * 
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, null)     = null
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(array1, null)   = cloned copy of array1
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, array2)   = cloned copy of array2
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([], [])         = []
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([null], [null]) = [null, null]
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(["a", "b", "c"], ["1", "2", "3"]) = ["a", "b", "c", "1", "2", "3"]
     *
* * @param array1 the first array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @param array2 the second array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @return The new array, null if both arrays are null. * The type of the new array is the type of the first array, * unless the first array is null, in which case the type is the same as the second array. * @since 2.1 "

Diagnosis:
The failing test `testJira567()` demonstrates two scenarios using `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)`:
1. Combining an array of Number with an array of Long works.
2. Combining an array of Integer with an array of Long throws an unexpected `ArrayStoreException`, instead of an `IllegalArgumentException` as expected by the test.

From the code snippet of the method `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)`, the method does the following:
- If one input array is null, it returns a clone of the other.
- Otherwise, it gets the component (element) type of the first array (`type1`).
- Creates a new array of type `type1` with the combined length.
- Copies elements from both input arrays into this new array using `System.arraycopy`.

The key point is the array type of the result is created based on the component type of the first array argument. `System.arraycopy` is used to copy elements from both arrays into this new array.

When the first array is `Number[]` and the second `Long[]`, `type1` is `Number`, so the new array is `Number[]`. Since `Long` is a subclass of `Number`, `System.arraycopy` copying `Long[]` elements into `Number[]` works fine.

When the first array is `Integer[]` and the second `Long[]`, `type1` is `Integer`. The new array is `Integer[]`. Copying `Long[]` elements into `Integer[]` results in an `ArrayStoreException` because a `Long` cannot be stored in an `Integer[]`.

The issue is that the method does not pre-check compatibility of the second array's element type with the component type of the first array. Instead, it relies on `System.arraycopy` which throws a low-level `ArrayStoreException` that is not descriptive of the usage error.

The current bug report notes that this resulting exception is not obvious and suggests it would be clearer if the method caught this incompatibility earlier and threw a more informative `IllegalArgumentException`. The failing test expects this behavior.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is that `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...)` does not check for mixed array element types compatibility before trying to copy, leading to uncaught `ArrayStoreException` rather than an explanatory `IllegalArgumentException`.

The recent bug reports are unrelated to this array type-checking issue.

Conclusion: The fault lies in `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...)` method's lack of pre-check for compatible array element types, resulting in `ArrayStoreException` instead of an informative exception when incompatible array types are passed. The test reveals this gap as it expects an `IllegalArgumentException` but sees `ArrayStoreException`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
